input: Write a business email in formal Japanese

keyUnknowns.whyItMatters: The subject and purpose of the email (e.g. inquiry, apology, request, follow-up) completely determines the content and structure of the email.
The recipient's role, seniority, and relationship to the sender determines the appropriate level of keigo (sonkeigo vs. kenjougo) and how to address them.
The industry and business context shapes the vocabulary, tone, and conventions used — a legal firm email differs greatly from a creative agency email.
The desired length or word count matters — a brief acknowledgment requires a very different structure from a detailed proposal email.
Whether the user wants a fully Japanese email, a bilingual version, or a Japanese draft with an English translation alongside affects the final deliverable format.
Any key details (names, company names, specific dates, figures) the email must include — without these, the draft will contain generic placeholders.
Whether the user prioritises ultra-formal traditional keigo or a modern professional tone determines how conservative or contemporary the language choices should be.

gold.taskTitle: Write a Formal Japanese Business Email
gold.taskDescription: Draft a business email in formal Japanese (keigo) for the user's specific professional purpose.

questions.title: What is the main purpose of this email?
questions.description: Identify the core action or message — e.g. making a request, sending an apology, following up on a meeting, introducing yourself, or responding to an inquiry.

questions.title: Who is the recipient relative to you?
questions.description: Clarify the recipient's role and relationship — e.g. a client, a senior executive at a partner company, a new business contact, or a colleague at another firm.

questions.title: What industry or business setting is this for?
questions.description: Understand the professional context — e.g. finance, technology, manufacturing, consulting — so that field-appropriate vocabulary and conventions can be applied.

questions.title: How long should the email be?
questions.description: Determine the expected length — a short 3-4 sentence acknowledgment, a standard single-page email, or a detailed multi-paragraph message.

questions.title: Do you need Japanese only, or with an English translation?
questions.description: Establish the output format — Japanese text only, a side-by-side bilingual version, or Japanese with an English translation below for reference.

questions.title: What specific names, dates, or details must be included?
questions.description: Gather concrete details — sender name, recipient name, company names, meeting dates, product names, or figures — that need to appear in the email.

questions.title: Should the tone be ultra-formal keigo or modern professional?
questions.description: Determine the register — highly traditional and ceremonial keigo versus a cleaner, contemporary formal style common in modern Japanese business communication.
